fullPassage: In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today's words, one could say that the pictures went "viral," and Doyle's endorsement gave the pictures "credibility." For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age. In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as "vertical reading." Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies. Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it's understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don't know how to verify information. This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever. Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading," which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight. For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information. Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author's claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently. As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire "fact-checkers" to evaluate their writers' claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading. Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so neither should the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.

det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'lateral reading, which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can' 일치

❌ ② 본문 'opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers' 일치

❌ ③ 본문 'Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author's claims' 일치

✅ ④ 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 본문 'They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously'에서 '여러 사이트를 동시에' 검토하도록 돕는 도구라고 했어요. '하나의 사이트만'은 정반대예요 ←정답
det.tip: 여러 사이트를 동시에 검토(review many sites simultaneously)가 사실입니다.

ch: 가로 읽기는 읽는 동안 가능한 한 많은 출처를 확인하며 정보를 검증하는 것이다.
한 학생은 통계를 접한 뒤 다른 탭을 열어 여러 출처로 그 수치를 검증할 수 있다.
디지털 가로 읽기를 하는 독자는 인터넷의 정보량을 이용해 저자 주장의 신뢰성을 확인할 수 있다.
가로 읽기는 한 번에 하나의 사이트만 검토하도록 돕는 도구를 사용하는 것이다.

questions.passage: In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today's words, one could say that the pictures went "viral," and Doyle's endorsement gave the pictures "credibility." For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age. In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 디지털 시대에 미디어 리터러시가 중요한 이유
det.analysis:
✅ ① why media literacy matters in the digital age(디지털 시대에 미디어 리터러시가 중요한 이유): 코팅리 일화로 시작해 세로·가로 읽기를 비교하며 정보 평가의 중요성을 다루는 글 전체를 아우름 ← 정답

❌ ② how to take photos that look completely real(진짜처럼 보이는 사진을 찍는 법): 도입 일화의 소재일 뿐 주제가 아님

❌ ③ the history of the printing press in Europe(유럽 인쇄기의 역사): 세로 읽기 배경 설명일 뿐임

❌ ④ a ranking of the most trusted news sites(가장 신뢰받는 뉴스 사이트 순위): 본문에 없는 내용
det.tip: 세로·가로 읽기를 관통하는 것 = 디지털 시대 미디어 리터러시의 중요성입니다.

det.korean: ③ 옆으로 읽기: 디지털 정보 검증하기
det.analysis:
글은 세로 읽기의 한계를 지적하고, 여러 출처를 교차 검증하는 '가로(옆으로) 읽기'로 정보를 평가하라고 강조해요.

questions.passage: Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: <u>information does not remain still</u>, so neither should the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 information does not remain still이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② 정보는 끊임없이 변하므로 독자도 계속 확인·평가해야 한다는 것
det.analysis:
밑줄 'information does not remain still(정보는 가만히 있지 않는다)'은 앞의 'the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving(세계와 정보 자체가 끊임없이 진화한다)'을 받는 표현이에요. 뒤에 'so neither should the reader(독자도 그래서는 안 된다)'가 이어져, 독자도 멈추지 말고 계속 평가해야 한다는 뜻이에요.

❌ ① 삭제 가능 여부에 관한 말이 아니에요.

✅ ② 정보가 계속 변하니 독자도 가로 읽기로 끊임없이 확인·평가해야 한다는 뜻이에요 ←정답

❌ ③ 전달 방식(조용함)에 관한 말이 아니에요.

❌ ④ 기록 매체(종이)에 관한 말이 아니에요.
det.tip: information does not remain still = 정보는 끊임없이 변한다 → 독자도 계속 평가해야 한다

ch: 정보는 한번 저장되면 결코 삭제할 수 없다는 것
정보는 끊임없이 변하므로 독자도 계속 확인하고 평가해야 한다는 것
정보는 언제나 조용하고 차분하게 전달된다는 것
정보는 반드시 종이에 기록해 두어야 한다는 것

questions.passage: For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in <u>her browser</u> and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information. Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author's claims.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 her가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ 인기 온라인 뉴스 기사를 읽는 한 학생
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장: 'she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser'. 앞 문장 'suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site'에서 소개한 '한 학생(a student)'을 she/her가 받아요.

✅ ④ 인기 온라인 뉴스 기사를 읽는 한 학생: her가 가리키는 바로 그 학생이에요 ←정답

❌ ① 사실 확인자는 뒤 단락의 다른 대상이에요.

❌ ② 기사를 쓴 저자는 학생이 읽는 대상일 뿐이에요.

❌ ③ 도일 경은 도입 일화의 인물이에요.
det.tip: a student reads an article → she / her browser로 이어집니다.

ch: 인기 온라인 뉴스 기사를 읽는 한 학생

questions.passage: Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes __________. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. det.analysis:

questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그 사진들은 소녀들이 요정들과 함께 노는 모습을 담고 있었다." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) The, the, fairies, girls, pictures, playing, showed, with 을 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies
det.analysis:
주어는 '그 사진들'이에요: The + pictures.

'~한 모습을 담고 있었다(보여 주었다)'는 과거 동사 showed로 써요: showed.

'소녀들이 요정들과 함께 노는'은 'the girls playing with fairies'로 이어요. show + 목적어 + 현재분사(~가 …하는 모습을 보여 주다) 구조예요: the + girls + playing + with + fairies.

순서대로 이으면 The / pictures / showed / the / girls / playing / with / fairies.
det.tip: show + 목적어 + 현재분사: showed the girls playing(소녀들이 노는 모습을 보여 주다)

det.korean: used (과거완료의 과거분사).
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'participants who had ___ less optimal strategies'에서 앞에 had가 있으므로 'had + 과거분사' 형태의 과거완료예요. 조사 시점(과거)보다 더 이전에 '덜 최적인 전략을 사용한' 일을 나타내므로, use를 과거분사 used로 바꿔야 해요. 'had used(사용했던)'로 해석돼요.
det.tip: had + 과거분사(과거완료): had used(사용했었다)

questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"거의 70년이 지나고 나서야 비로소 그 소녀들은 (모든 것이 꾸며낸 일이었다고) 인정했다." (10단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) admit, after, almost, did, finally, girls, Only, seventy, the, years 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것 (부사구 도치 구문 활용)

det.korean: Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit
det.analysis:
'거의 70년이 지나고 나서야'라는 제한의 부사구가 문장 맨 앞에 와요: Only + after + almost + seventy + years.

부정·제한의 부사구가 문두에 오면 주어와 (조)동사가 도치돼요. 그래서 'did + 주어 + 동사원형'으로 써요: did + the + girls + finally + admit.

순서대로 이으면 Only / after / almost / seventy / years / did / the / girls / finally / admit.
det.tip: Only + 부사구 문두 → 도치(did + 주어 + 동사원형): did the girls finally admit

questions.wa: Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit
accept: Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit

questions.passage: However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies. Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it's understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. __________? In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don't know how to verify information. This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"첨단 기술이 지금 사람들이 속는 것을 막아 주는가?"

[ advanced / being / Does / fooled / from / now / people / prevent / technology ] (9단어) (영어로)

det.korean: Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now
det.analysis:
일반동사 현재 의문문이라 'Does + 주어 + 동사원형'으로 시작해요. 주어는 '첨단 기술'이에요: Does + advanced + technology + prevent.

'prevent A from -ing(A가 ~하는 것을 막다)' 구문을 써요. '사람들이 속는 것을'은 people from being fooled로 이어요: people + from + being + fooled.

'지금'은 now로 마무리해요: now.

순서대로 이으면 Does / advanced / technology / prevent / people / from / being / fooled / now.
det.tip: Does + 주어 + 동사원형 + prevent A from being p.p.(A가 ~당하는 것을 막다)

questions.wa: Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now
accept: Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now

questions.passage: Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author's claims. __________. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently. As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire "fact-checkers" to evaluate their writers' claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그들은 여러 사이트를 동시에 검토하도록 도와주는 인터넷 브라우저 도구를 활용할 수 있다." (12단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) browser, can, help, Internet, many, review, simultaneously, sites, that, They, tools, utilize 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 12단어로 쓸 것 (주격 관계대명사 that 활용)

det.korean: They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously
det.analysis:
주어와 동사는 '그들은 활용할 수 있다'예요: They + can + utilize.

무엇을 활용하는가 하면 '인터넷 브라우저 도구'예요: Internet + browser + tools.

이 도구를 꾸며 주는 '~하도록 도와주는'은 주격 관계대명사 that으로 이어요. 선행사 tools를 받아 'that help review ~'로 써요: that + help + review.

'여러 사이트를 동시에'는 many sites simultaneously로 마무리해요: many + sites + simultaneously.

순서대로 이으면 They / can / utilize / Internet / browser / tools / that / help / review / many / sites / simultaneously.
det.tip: 선행사(tools) + 주격 관계대명사 that + 동사(help): ~하도록 도와주는 도구

questions.wa: They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously
accept: They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously
